article.title: Why a Good KPI Can Still Create Bad Behavior
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

sources.label: Harvard Business Review - performance measurement background

paragraphs.en:
A key performance indicator is designed to make an important business goal measurable. Revenue growth, customer response time, defect rates, conversion, and employee utilization can all be useful KPIs. The problem begins when people stop treating the metric as evidence about performance and start treating the metric itself as the goal. A measure can then improve while the underlying business outcome becomes worse.

Imagine a customer-support center measured mainly by average handling time. Managers want faster service, so the KPI seems reasonable. Employees soon learn that short calls are rewarded. They may rush customers, transfer difficult cases, or close conversations before the real problem is solved. Average handling time falls, yet repeat contacts and customer frustration rise. The team has improved the measured number without improving the service.

This pattern appears because employees respond rationally to incentives. When bonuses, rankings, or management attention depend heavily on one number, people naturally search for actions that move that number. Some actions create genuine value, but others only improve the measurement. The stronger the pressure on a narrow KPI, the more important it becomes to examine unintended behavior around it.

Sales targets provide another example. A company may reward the number of new contracts. Salespeople can increase that number by offering large discounts or signing customers who are unlikely to stay. New contracts rise, but margin and retention may deteriorate. A better measurement system could combine acquisition with profitability, cancellation, or customer quality instead of assuming that every new contract has equal value.

The answer is not to eliminate KPIs. Organizations need measures to coordinate work and identify problems. Instead, managers should connect each KPI to the business outcome it is supposed to represent. They can ask: What behavior would improve this number without improving the real objective? What important quality is missing? Could employees shift work to another team? Could the metric encourage short-term gains at the expense of long-term value?

Balanced measures can reduce these risks, but adding many metrics creates another problem. If a dashboard contains thirty indicators, employees may not know what matters. A practical approach is to choose a small number of primary outcomes and use secondary guardrail metrics to detect harmful side effects. For customer support, handling time might remain useful, while repeat-contact rate and customer satisfaction act as guardrails.

Managers should also review a KPI when behavior changes. A measure that worked during one stage of a business may become inappropriate after the operating model changes. Metrics are management tools, not permanent laws. Their definitions, incentives, and consequences need periodic review.

A good KPI therefore does more than move in the desired direction. It should encourage behavior that remains aligned with the underlying objective. When a metric improves unusually quickly, managers should celebrate carefully and investigate how the improvement was achieved. The most important question is not simply, 'Did the KPI improve?' It is, 'Did the business become better in the way this KPI was meant to represent?'
paragraphs.zh: KPI 的目的是把重要業務目標變得可衡量，但當人們把指標本身當成最終目標時，就可能出現數字變好、真正成果反而惡化的情況。例如客服只追求平均處理時間，員工可能匆忙結束通話，導致重複聯絡與不滿增加；業務只追新合約數，也可能透過大幅折扣或低品質客戶達標。解法不是取消 KPI，而是把 KPI 與真正 business outcome 連結，思考哪些行為能讓數字改善卻沒有創造價值。可以用少量主要 outcome 搭配 guardrail metrics，並定期檢查定義與 incentive 是否仍適合目前營運模式。
paragraphs.ja: KPIは重要なbusiness goalを測定可能にしますが、metric自体がgoalになると、数字だけ改善して本来の成果が悪化することがあります。たとえばcustomer supportがaverage handling timeだけを追えば、難しい案件を転送したり早く終了したりして、repeat contactや不満が増える可能性があります。salesでも新規契約数だけを追うとdiscountや低品質顧客が増えることがあります。KPIをなくすのではなく、本来のbusiness outcomeとの関係を確認し、harmful side effectを検知するguardrail metricを置きます。また事業モデルが変わればKPIも定期的に見直す必要があります。

quiz.question: How can a KPI improve while service worsens?
quiz.answer: People may optimize the measured number rather than the real outcome.
